props.gloss_en: R' Eliezer b'R' Yosei HaGelili expounds: 'the Lord blessed Oved-edom the Gittite ... because of the ark of God' (II Sam 6:12) -- blessed for honouring the ark, which neither ate nor drank, but before which he swept and sprinkled
one who hosts a Torah scholar in his home, feeds him, gives him drink and lets him benefit from his possessions -- all the more so [is he blessed]
[asked: what is the blessing with which he was blessed?] Rav Yehuda bar Zevida: it is Chamot and her eight daughters-in-law, who bore six each in a single womb

as it is said: 'Peulletai the eighth' and it is written 'for God blessed him' (I Chr 26:5); 'all these of the sons of Oved-edom, they and their sons and their brethren, able men in strength for the service, sixty-two of Oved-edom' (I Chr 26:8)
R' Avin HaLevi: whoever forces the moment -- the moment forces him
and whoever yields before the moment -- the moment yields before him
Rav Yosef was 'Sinai' and Rabba 'uprooter of mountains'; the moment needed them. They sent there: Sinai or uprooter of mountains -- which takes precedence? They sent back: Sinai takes precedence
for everyone needs the owner of the wheat
the Chaldeans to Rav Yosef: you will reign two years
even so Rav Yosef did not accept [the headship], because the Chaldeans had told him: you will reign two years
Rabba reigned twenty-two years; Rav Yosef reigned two and a half years
all those years that Rabba reigned, [Rav Yosef] did not even call a bloodletter to his house
